title: Prokaryote vs eukaryote
lines: | Feature | Prokaryote | Eukaryote
| Nucleus | none; DNA in nucleoid | membrane-bound nucleus
| DNA | circular, no histones; plasmids | linear, with histones
| Ribosomes | 70S | 80S in cytoplasm
| Wall | peptidoglycan | plants cellulose; fungi chitin; animals none
| Organelles | no mitochondria, ER, Golgi | present
| Division | binary fission | mitosis and meiosis
! Mitochondria and chloroplasts have 70S ribosomes and circular DNA, like bacteria.

title: Organelles and their jobs
lines: | Organelle | Job
| Nucleolus | makes rRNA; assembles ribosomes
| Rough ER | proteins for export
| Smooth ER | lipids and steroids; detox in liver
| Golgi | modifies, packages, secretes; makes lysosomes
| Lysosome | digestive enzymes; autophagy
| Mitochondrion | aerobic respiration (Krebs in matrix, ETC on cristae)
| Chloroplast | photosynthesis (light stage in grana, Calvin cycle in stroma)
| Centriole | spindle in animal cells
Secretory route: RER → vesicle → Golgi → secretory vesicle → cell membrane.

title: Carbohydrates at a glance
lines: | Sugar | Made of | Note
| Maltose | glucose + glucose | from starch digestion
| Sucrose | glucose + fructose | non-reducing; moves in phloem
| Lactose | glucose + galactose | milk sugar
| Starch | α-glucose | plant store; iodine → blue-black
| Glycogen | α-glucose, highly branched | animal store: liver and muscle
| Cellulose | β-glucose, unbranched | plant cell wall
| Chitin | modified glucose (with nitrogen) | insect skeleton, fungal wall
! Glucose and fructose are both C₆H₁₂O₆: isomers. Humans cannot digest cellulose.

title: Four levels of protein structure
lines: | Level | What it is | Held by
| Primary | amino acid sequence | peptide bonds
| Secondary | α-helix or β-pleated sheet | hydrogen bonds
| Tertiary | 3-D folding of one chain | disulphide, ionic, hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic forces
| Quaternary | two or more chains | same as tertiary; e.g. haemoglobin 2α + 2β
- n amino acids in one chain → n − 1 peptide bonds, n − 1 water molecules lost.
! Denaturing (heat, wrong pH) destroys the 3-D shape but not the primary sequence.

title: DNA numbers
lines: - Watson and Crick, 1953 (X-ray data from Franklin and Wilkins).
- A = T (2 hydrogen bonds); G ≡ C (3 hydrogen bonds).
- Chargaff: A + G = T + C = 50 %.
- Strands antiparallel; 10 base pairs per turn; 3.4 nm per turn.
- Replication is semi-conservative (Meselson and Stahl).
! RNA has ribose and uracil; Chargaff's rule does not apply to single-stranded RNA.

title: Enzymes: how they work
lines: - Biological catalysts, mostly proteins; lower activation energy; not used up.
- Lock and key: Fischer. Induced fit: Koshland.
- Rate rises with temperature to an optimum (about 37 °C in humans), then falls as the enzyme denatures.
- More substrate: rate levels off when all active sites are full.
| Cofactor | Nature | Example
| Prosthetic group | organic, tightly bound | haem
| Coenzyme | organic, loosely bound | NAD⁺, FAD
| Activator | metal ion | Mg²⁺, Zn²⁺
Optimum pH: pepsin about 2, salivary amylase 6.8, pancreatic lipase about 9.

title: Enzyme inhibitors
lines: | Type | Binds to | More substrate helps?
| Competitive | active site; looks like substrate | yes
| Non-competitive | another site; changes shape | no
| Irreversible | enzyme, by strong bonds | no; enzyme lost
Feedback inhibition: the end product switches off the first enzyme of its own pathway.
! Strong inhibition at low substrate that vanishes at high substrate = competitive.

title: Respiration: where and how much
lines: | Stage | Site | Per glucose
| Glycolysis | cytoplasm | 2 pyruvate, net 2 ATP, 2 NADH
| Link reaction | matrix | 2 acetyl CoA, 2 CO₂, 2 NADH
| Krebs cycle (2 turns) | matrix | 4 CO₂, 6 NADH, 2 FADH₂, 2 ATP
| ETC | inner membrane (cristae) | most ATP; O₂ + H⁺ → H₂O
- Aerobic total: about 36-38 ATP per glucose.
- No O₂: muscle → lactic acid; yeast → ethanol + CO₂; net 2 ATP.
! O₂ is the final electron acceptor. Cyanide blocks the chain.

title: Photosynthesis in two stages
lines: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (light, chlorophyll)
| Stage | Site | In | Out
| Light-dependent | thylakoids (grana) | light, H₂O, ADP, NADP⁺ | O₂, ATP, NADPH
| Calvin cycle | stroma | CO₂, ATP, NADPH | sugar (via PGAL)
- Rubisco fixes CO₂ onto RuBP (5C) → 2 PGA (3C).
- Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light best; green is reflected.
! The O₂ released comes from water (photolysis), not from CO₂.

title: Classification and the kingdoms
lines: Ranks, largest to smallest: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.
Mnemonic: King Philip Came Over For Good Soup (Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species).
- Binomial name (Linnaeus): Genus capital, species small, in italics: Homo sapiens.
| Kingdom (Whittaker, 1969) | Examples
| Monera | bacteria, cyanobacteria
| Protista | Amoeba, Paramecium, Plasmodium, algae
| Fungi | yeast, Penicillium, mushroom
| Plantae | moss, fern, pine, mango
| Animalia | sponge to mammals
! Viruses are in no kingdom: acellular, DNA or RNA, reproduce only in a host cell.

title: Plant groups and monocot vs dicot
lines: | Group | Vascular? | Seeds? | Example
| Bryophytes | no | no | moss
| Pteridophytes | yes | no | fern
| Gymnosperms | yes | naked | pine
| Angiosperms | yes | in fruit | wheat, mango
| Feature | Monocot | Dicot
| Cotyledons | one | two
| Veins | parallel | net
| Flower parts | threes | fours or fives
| Roots | fibrous | tap root
! Mosses: gametophyte dominant and need water for fertilisation. Ferns onwards: sporophyte dominant.

title: Animal phyla with examples
lines: | Phylum | Hallmark | Example
| Porifera | pores | sponge
| Cnidaria | stinging cells | Hydra, jellyfish
| Platyhelminthes | flatworms | tapeworm, liver fluke
| Nematoda | roundworms | Ascaris
| Annelida | segmented worms | earthworm, leech
| Arthropoda | jointed legs, chitin | insects, spiders, crabs
| Mollusca | soft body, shell | snail, octopus
| Echinodermata | spiny skin, tube feet | starfish
| Chordata | notochord | fish to mammals
Heart chambers: fish 2, amphibians 3, reptiles 3 (crocodile 4), birds 4, mammals 4.

title: Ecology essentials
lines: - Producers → primary → secondary → tertiary consumers; decomposers recycle.
- 10 % rule: 10,000 kJ in producers → 1,000 → 100 → 10 kJ.
| Interaction | Effect | Example
| Mutualism | +/+ | lichen; Rhizobium + legume
| Commensalism | +/0 | orchid on a tree
| Parasitism | +/− | tapeworm in a human
| Predation | +/− (prey dies) | hawk and sparrow
- Nitrogen: fixation (Rhizobium), nitrification (Nitrosomonas then Nitrobacter), denitrification (back to N₂).
- Acid rain: SO₂ and NOₓ. Ozone damage: CFCs. Greenhouse: CO₂, methane.

title: Digestive enzymes
lines: | Enzyme | Made by | Acts on → gives
| Salivary amylase | salivary glands | starch → maltose
| Pepsin | stomach (as pepsinogen) | protein → polypeptides
| Trypsin | pancreas (as trypsinogen) | protein → peptides
| Pancreatic lipase | pancreas | fat → fatty acids + glycerol
| Maltase, sucrase, lactase | small intestine wall | disaccharides → monosaccharides
| Peptidases | small intestine wall | peptides → amino acids
! HCl activates pepsinogen; enterokinase activates trypsinogen. Bile has no enzyme: it emulsifies fat.
- Gastrin (stomach); secretin and cholecystokinin (duodenum).

title: Heart and vessels
lines: - Right side: right atrium → tricuspid → right ventricle → pulmonary artery.
- Left side: pulmonary veins → left atrium → bicuspid (mitral) → left ventricle → aorta.
- Impulse: SA node → AV node → bundle of His → Purkinje fibres.
- Lubb = AV valves close; dub = semilunar valves close.
- At 75 beats/min: cycle 0.8 s = atrial systole 0.1 + ventricular systole 0.3 + diastole 0.4.
| Vessel | Wall | Valves
| Artery | thick, elastic | no
| Vein | thin | yes
| Capillary | one cell thick | no
! Pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood; pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood.

title: Breathing, gases and lung volumes
lines: - Breathing in: diaphragm contracts and flattens; external intercostals lift ribs.
- O₂: about 97 % as oxyhaemoglobin. CO₂: about 70 % as bicarbonate.
- CO binds haemoglobin about 200 times more strongly than O₂.
| Volume | Typical adult
| Tidal volume | 500 mL
| Inspiratory reserve | 3,000 mL
| Expiratory reserve | 1,100 mL
| Residual volume | 1,200 mL
- Vital capacity = TV + IRV + ERV. Total lung capacity = VC + RV.
! Residual volume is not part of vital capacity. Breathing centre: medulla, driven mainly by CO₂.

title: Down the nephron
lines: - Glomerulus → Bowman's capsule: ultrafiltration (no cells, no plasma proteins).
- Proximal tubule: reabsorbs all glucose and amino acids, most water and salts.
- Loop of Henle: concentrates the medulla so water can be drawn out.
- Distal tubule: aldosterone → more Na⁺ reabsorbed.
- Collecting duct: ADH → more water reabsorbed, less urine.
- Kidney → ureter → bladder → urethra.
! Urea is made in the liver; the kidney only removes it. Glucose in urine suggests diabetes mellitus; protein suggests glomerular damage.

title: Nerves and the brain
lines: - Resting potential about −70 mV. Depolarisation: Na⁺ in. Repolarisation: K⁺ out.
- All-or-none; myelinated fibres conduct fastest (node to node).
- Synapse: acetylcholine crosses the gap; one-way transmission.
- Reflex arc: receptor → sensory → relay → motor neuron → effector.
| Part | Job
| Cerebrum | thought, memory, voluntary action
| Cerebellum | balance, coordination
| Medulla | breathing, heart rate
| Hypothalamus | temperature, thirst; controls pituitary
! Myopia: image in front of retina, concave lens. Hypermetropia: behind retina, convex lens.

title: Hormones to know
lines: | Gland | Hormone | Job
| Anterior pituitary | GH, TSH, FSH, LH | growth; controls other glands
| Posterior pituitary | ADH, oxytocin | water reabsorption; labour
| Thyroid | thyroxine | metabolic rate (needs iodine)
| Pancreas | insulin / glucagon | lowers / raises blood glucose
| Adrenal medulla | adrenaline | fight or flight
| Testes | testosterone | male characters
| Ovaries | oestrogen, progesterone | female characters; uterus lining
! Too little iodine → goitre. Too little insulin → diabetes mellitus. Too little ADH → diabetes insipidus.

title: Immunity
lines: Antibody classes: GAMED (IgG, IgA, IgM, IgE, IgD).
| Class | Key fact
| IgG | most abundant; crosses the placenta
| IgA | in milk, saliva, tears
| IgM | first made; largest (pentamer)
| IgE | allergy
| IgD | B-cell surface receptor
- B cells → plasma cells → antibodies (humoral). T cells mature in the thymus (cell-mediated).
| Immunity | Natural | Artificial
| Active | after infection | vaccination
| Passive | mother's milk, placenta | injected antibodies
! HIV destroys helper T cells, so both arms of immunity fail.

title: Reproduction
lines: Sperm path, SEVEN UP: Seminiferous tubules, Epididymis, Vas deferens, Ejaculatory duct, (Nothing), Urethra, Penis.
| Days (28-day cycle) | Event | Hormones
| 1-5 | menstruation | oestrogen and progesterone low
| 6-13 | follicle grows; lining rebuilds | FSH → oestrogen rises
| about 14 | ovulation | LH surge
| 15-28 | corpus luteum; lining ready | progesterone high
- Fertilisation happens in the oviduct (Fallopian tube).
- 1 primary spermatocyte → 4 sperm; 1 primary oocyte → 1 egg + polar bodies.
! Gametes have 23 chromosomes; body cells 46.

title: Mendel's ratios and gametes
lines: | Cross | Phenotypes | Genotypes
| RrYy × RrYy | 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 | 9 kinds
| Incomplete dominance F₂ | 1 : 2 : 1 | 1 : 2 : 1
- Gamete types = 2ⁿ (n = heterozygous pairs): AaBbCc → 8.
- Product rule: chance of rryy from RrYy × RrYy = ¼ × ¼ = 1/16.
! Of the tall F₂ plants from Tt × Tt, 2/3 are heterozygous.

title: Sex linkage, blood groups and syndromes
lines: - X-linked recessive (haemophilia, colour blindness): more common in males.
- Father never passes an X-linked allele to his son.
- Carrier mother × normal father: ½ sons affected, ½ daughters carriers.
| Group | Genotypes
| A | IA IA, IA i
| B | IB IB, IB i
| AB | IA IB (codominance)
| O | i i
| Syndrome | Chromosomes
| Down | trisomy 21 (47)
| Klinefelter | XXY male (47)
| Turner | XO female (45)

title: Genetic code and biotechnology
lines: - 64 codons, 20 amino acids: triplet, degenerate, nearly universal.
- Start: AUG. Stop: UAA, UAG, UGA.
- Transcription: DNA → mRNA (nucleus). Translation: mRNA → protein (ribosome).
| Tool | Job
| Restriction enzyme | cuts DNA at a set sequence
| DNA ligase | joins DNA pieces
| Plasmid | vector that carries a gene into bacteria
| PCR (Taq polymerase) | copies DNA: 2ⁿ copies after n cycles
| Gel electrophoresis | sorts DNA by size; DNA fingerprinting
- Products: human insulin from E. coli; Bt cotton; Dolly the sheep (1996, cloned from an adult cell).

title: Evolution
lines: | Point | Lamarck | Darwin
| Idea | use and disuse; acquired characters inherited | natural selection of inherited variation
| Book | Philosophie Zoologique (1809) | On the Origin of Species (1859)
| Status | rejected | accepted
- Homologous organs: same structure, different job (human arm, bat wing, whale flipper).
- Analogous organs: same job, different origin (bird and insect wings).
- Vestigial: human appendix.
- Hardy-Weinberg: p + q = 1; p² + 2pq + q² = 1.
- Miller and Urey (1953): sparks in CH₄, NH₃, H₂, H₂O → amino acids.
! Herbert Spencer, not Darwin, coined "survival of the fittest".
